page: Amazon Web Services m7a.48xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 192 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the AWS Nitro hypervisor and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the m7a.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark CPU scores, and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Its memory subsystem exhibits exceptional throughput, with read and write bandwidths reaching top-tier levels. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are highly advanced, supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512 and AES, which translate to top-tier performance in PassMark encryption and extended instruction tests.

The instance shows varying performance in language model tasks. While prompt processing speeds for small, medium, and large LLM models rank in the top 10%, text generation speeds are more moderate, with the small model text generation falling into the bottom 25%. Additionally, single-core performance and database operations register in the top 25%. These characteristics make the instance highly efficient for massive multi-threaded workloads, software compilation, static web serving, and Redis operations, while presenting a resource-dense profile for general-purpose enterprise applications.
